title: Against Vorstius: God only in heaven by substance — rejected

pass_b_english: Therefore Conrad Vorstius errs, deceived by Scotus, Bodin, and Taurellus, in Notes on Disputation III On God p. 232, because against the catholic consensus and the most learned Zanchi he teaches that God according to His substance is nowhere but in heaven. He alleges seven reasons.

But that error is from a double confusion: it does not distinguish Scripture's proper from improper speech about throne and dwelling; and from the aspect of special presence it overturns the very immensity of essence. For God is in a special ratio in Christ's humanity by hypostatic union, in the saints by knowledge and love, in the Church by help, in heaven by majesty and glory — the immensity of essence nonetheless remaining everywhere.
source_text: ERRAT igitur CONR. VORSTIUS a Scoto, Bodino, Taurello deceptus, Notis ad disp. III. p.232 de Deo, quia contra catholicum consensum et doctissimum Zanchium docet, Deum secundum substantiam suam non esse alibi quam in caelo. Allegrat rationes septem. VERUM error iste a duplici confusione est: non distinguit sermonis divini potentiam propriam ab impropria de throno et habitatione; et a specialis praesentiae aspectu ipsam immensitatem essentiae evertit. Deus enim speciali ratione in humanitate Christi per unionem hypostaticam, in sanctis per cognitionem et amorem, in Ecclesia per auxilium, in caelo per majestatem et gloriam — manente tamen essentiae immensitate ubique.
